definition: A shortcut connection that adds a layer's input directly to its output, helping gradients flow through very deep networks.
details: Residual (or 'skip') connections, popularized by ResNet, are a core building block of transformer layers and make it feasible to train networks with dozens or hundreds of layers.

explainer.lead: It adds a layer's input directly to its output, letting gradients flow through very deep networks. It matters because it made networks with dozens or hundreds of layers trainable and is a core building block of transformer layers.

tiers.eli5: Like a staircase with a side ramp, so you can still get to the top even if the stairs are steep.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wrap blocks so output equals block(input) plus input, which stabilises training of deep stacks. A pitfall is that dimensions must match, so projections or padding are needed when they differ.
tiers.paperLevel: A block computes y = F(x) + x, so gradients pass through the identity path; popularised by ResNet and now standard in transformer layers. It enables training of networks with dozens or hundreds of layers, though very deep stacks can still face optimisation issues.

explainer.example: A transformer sublayer computes its attention output, adds the original input to it, then normalises, so the signal has a direct path around the sublayer.

citation.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
